Your money brain peaks at fifty-three.
Too young? Too old? Either way, you pay more.
Researchers checked ten kinds of loans and card fees.
Young and old borrowers paid higher rates and more fees.
On home equity lines, twenty-five-year-olds paid about two ninety-five a year more than fifty-year-olds.
Seventy-five-year-olds? About two hundred sixty-five more.
Experience grows. Quick thinking fades. Around fifty-three, they cross.
So at any age: borrow slowly, and compare twice.
